subject: Estimate explained variance in an ordered categorical model

messages.author: f42b0240615306ac
messages.subject: Estimate explained variance in an ordered categorical model
parts:
Hi Stan, 

I am using the ordered_logistic() function to model an ordered categorical variable over several exploratory covariates. The model follows as below:
y ~ ordered_logistic(beta1 * x1 + beta2 * x2, cut)

But, I am stuck in computing explained variance by each covariate from the STAN estimation. Could anyone guide me in how to do so?

Thanks,

Xulong

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Estimate explained variance in an ordered categorical model
parts:
What do you mean by explained variance for an ordered categorical
outcome? Being from computer science, I tend to think information
theoretically for categorical variables, so maybe something like
information gain as expalined here:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explained_variation

Of course, you'll get a posterior distribution over such things
in a Bayesian model, or you could try to calculate from an estimator
like the posterior mean or median.

- Bob
